evidence.detail: The class recognizes @hov@/@shi@ plus <hover>, <shift>, </hover>, </shift>, </lift> and signed <lift=N> markup; lift magnitude is clamped to 40.
It computes time-varying sinusoidal integer offsets with amplitudes 2 and 3 pixels. The live font renderer applies one to x and the other to y, then subtracts the parsed lift offset.
Whenever hover/shift motion is rendered, the font path arms this class's timer; its predicate keeps redraw active for 100 ms and then emits one final invalidation transition.
rs/l/h is the live consumer of the parser and offset functions, applying them to glyphs, sprites and embedded rich-text elements.

candidates.note: Descriptive exact-v308 name for hover/shift/lift rich-text motion processing.

evidence.detail: The class recognizes @par@ and numbered @par2@..@par8@ forms, <par>/<parN> open/close forms, explicit <par=color> values, and pimg/pNimg particle-image tags.
Its render helper constructs recovered R204 OverlayParticle instances, configures direction, motion, size, opacity/color and lifetime, then submits them to OverlayParticleManager.
The live rs/l/h renderer uses the parsed par style, pimg style/id and per-string trigger positions to decide when and where to spawn those particles around rendered text/images.
A per-string/position timestamp map suppresses repeated particle generation within a 50 ms window, proving this class owns the runtime rich-text particle emission policy.

candidates.note: Descriptive exact-v308 name for par/pimg markup that emits R204 overlay particles.
